'''Hildreth–Lu estimation''', named for [[Clifford Hildreth]] and [[John Y. Lu]],<ref>{{cite journal |last=Hildreth |first= C. |last2=Lu |first2=J. Y. |title=Demand Relations with Autocorrelated Disturbances |journal=Technical Bulletin |volume=276 |publisher=Michigan State University Agricultural Experiment Station |date=November 1960 }}</ref> is a method for adjusting a [[linear model]] in response to the presence of [[serial correlation]] in the [[error term]]. It is an iterative procedure related to the [[Cochrane–Orcutt estimation]].

The idea is to repeatedly apply [[ordinary least squares]] to
:<math>y_t - \rho y_{t-1} = \alpha(1-\rho)+(X_t - \rho X_{t-1})\beta + e_t \,</math>
for different values of <math>\rho</math> between −1 and 1. From all these auxiliary regressions, one selects the pair ''(α, β)'' that yields the smallest [[residual sum of squares]].
